title: refactor(ci): simplify workflows, bump actions & deps, improve cache parallelism
author: Samir Patel
description:
Motivation: The monorepo has accumulated >20 separate workflow files with significant duplication across lint/test/release jobs. This increases maintenance burden, causes inconsistent caching, and made it hard to reason about parallelism and GH Actions billing. This PR consolidates per-repo workflows into a small set of reusable workflows, bumps critical Actions and platform deps, and implements safer caching/parallelism defaults to reduce CI costs and flakiness.

What this change does (single continuous description): Consolidate lint/test/release flows into three reusable workflows under .github/workflows (lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml) and add .github/workflows/common.yml for shared jobs and templates. Introduce a reusable matrix strategy for lint/test to reduce duplication, and add a lightweight integration job that runs only on changed packages to speed iteration. Bump core GH Actions and platform runtimes: actions/checkout@v4 (pinned to v4@sha256), actions/setup-node to v4 (default node 20), actions/cache improvements with custom cache key helper to mitigate key collisions; pin several community actions to SHAs. Upgrade Node.js versions used in CI to 20.x where safe, fall back to 18 for legacy test matrices where necessary. Add setup for go and python actions to use pinned versions for release workflows.

Hygiene & security: replace floating action tags with SHA pinned refs for high-risk actions, update CONTRIBUTING.md CI badges and docs references, and add a short note in SECURITY.md about pinned actions.

Performance & reliability: implement parallelism limits for ephemeral self-hosted runners to avoid noisy neighbors, add a cache warmup step for large monorepo dependency caches, and use a small script scripts/cache-utils.sh to compute stable keys based on package-lock.json/yarn.lock and workspace metadata. This reduces cache miss rate observed in daily runs.

Testing & rollout: The change was rolled out in two phases: phase 1 (lint/test consolidation + caching) merged to main and monitored for 48h; phase 2 (release automation and pinning) merged after a follow-up addressing a Windows runner edge-case. See CI summary below.

Checklist: 
- [x] Consolidate workflows and add reusable templates
- [x] Bump actions and pin SHAs for high-risk actions
- [x] Implement cache key helper and warming
- [x] Add docs/CONTRIBUTING and SECURITY updates
- [x] Verify on main with staged runs and fix Windows path escaping issue

References: Linear ENG-1213 (CI hygiene), ENG-1300 (reduce CI costs), example reuse from docs: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/reusing-workflows

Notes: description is intentionally concise; detailed implementation notes are in commit messages and changed files. If anything in release automation looks risky we can revert the release workflow independently since it's isolated behind its own reusable workflow.
